questions.q: Why are practice and feedback so important in a workshop?
options: Because a workshop is not simply a source of information but the starting point for developing a new skill
Because instructors are graded on them
questions.explain: Learners move from novice towards competence by practising and getting feedback.
questions.evidence: a Carpentries workshop is not simply a source of information: It is the starting point for development of a new skill.

options: The memory you use to actively think about things
questions.explain: Working memory is small, so cognitive load must be managed carefully.
questions.evidence: This is the type of memory you use to actively think about things and is often called working memory.

questions.q: What is formative assessment used for during workshops?
options: To track learners' progress and adjust the teaching as needed
To grade learners for a certificate
To rank learners against each other
To decide who may attend the next workshop
questions.explain: Short checks during teaching reveal misunderstandings early.
questions.evidence: We use formative assessment of learners during workshops to help track learners' progress and adjust our approach to teaching the content as needed.

questions.q: Like all other skills, what does good teaching require?
questions.explain: The belief that good teachers are simply born is wrong.
questions.evidence: Like all other skills, good teaching requires practice and feedback.

questions.q: Which two tendencies should structured feedback on teaching help overcome?
options: Speaking too fast and too quietly
Focusing only on content (though delivery matters as much) and giving only negative or only positive feedback
questions.explain: Balanced feedback on content and delivery is the most useful.
questions.evidence: This helps overcome two common tendencies when giving feedback on teaching: to focus on the content (even though delivery is at least as important) and to either provide only negative or only positive feedback.

questions.q: What does live coding force the instructor to do?
questions.explain: Going at typing speed gives learners time to follow along.
questions.evidence: Live coding forces the instructor to slow down.

questions.q: How is participatory live coding different from teaching from a slide deck?
options: A slide deck is like a railway track; live coding lets instructors go off-road and follow learners' interests
questions.explain: Learners also see how experts deal with mistakes.
questions.evidence: Where a slide deck is like a railway track, participatory live coding allows instructors to go off-road and follow their learners' interests.

questions.q: What is arguably the most important outcome an instructor can achieve?
options: Covering every topic in the lesson
Cultivating learners' motivation to continue learning
questions.explain: Motivated learners keep building the skill after the workshop.
questions.evidence: cultivating motivation to continue learning, and to carefully pursue best-practices in doing so, is arguably the most important outcome we can achieve

options: Making a lesson shorter for everyone
Changing things to serve an individual with a demonstrated need
questions.explain: Universal design goes further, building accessibility in for everyone from the start.
questions.evidence: Accessibility support means changing things to serve an individual with a demonstrated need (also known as accommodations).

questions.q: What is one of the greatest strengths of Carpentries workshops?
options: They are prepared and run by more than one person
questions.explain: Never teach alone: helpers support learners while the instructor teaches.
questions.evidence: workshops are prepared and executed by more than one person.
